_comment: Bases, affixes and drop rules. Every base has an itemClass (itemClasses); an affix only rolls on the classes or class groups in its 'on' list, so bonuses make sense for the item (no blade skills on a bow, no attack speed on boots, no movement speed on gloves). Uniques and set items are hand-made (uniques, sets) and ignore those rules: same base, name and lines every time, only min–max ranges roll. guardEfficiency (shields) reduces the Energy spent per block; blockReduction (shields) adds to the share of a blocked hit the guard stops (balance.json guard). level = minimum item level (iLvl) for the base/affix to appear. size = inventory cells [width, height]. inventory = backpack grid (columns × rows); for now it limits how many items the character carries. startingGear = bases a new character wears; startingBackpack = bases it carries. twoHanded (bows, great weapons) = takes both hands: no shield and no second weapon. attackSpeedPct = the weapon's own attack speed (great weapons swing slower). Maces (itemClass mace, tag mace) feed Maces; great weapons (itemClass great, tag great) feed Two-Handed. rangeTiles = how far a bow shoots (14 tiles reach the edge of a 1280x720 screen). rareNames = parts of rare item names: '<first> <second>'. Wands (slot 'wand', worn in either hand: with a shield, or beside a weapon) carry a spell: while worn it adds spellLevel to that spell and lets you cast it even before you unlock it in the tree (skills.json). uniques/sets: props are {stat, value} (fixed) or {stat, min, max} (rolled when it drops); level = minimum item level; weight = how often it is picked among the allowed ones. A set's bonuses add up as more different pieces are worn (2 pieces, 3 pieces…).

trade._comment: Vendor prices. Item price = (basePrice + perItemLevel x iLvl + perAffix x lines) x rarityMult[rarity] (normal, magic, rare, set, unique); the vendor pays sellFraction of that. The stock (stockSize items, normal and magic only, iLvl = character level) is rolled again every time you come to town. Consumables cost their own 'price'. npcRangeTiles = how close you must stand to trade or use the stash.

consumables._comment: Used from the HUD keys (ui/keys.json). restore = life | energy, pctOfMax of the maximum given over 'seconds' (several potions stack). cooldownSeconds = time before the same kind can be used again. belt = how many you carry is limited: beltWithout of each kind with no belt, plus the worn belt's beltSlots (a full belt leaves potions on the ground). price 0 = not sold. dropChance = rank → chance of one more when a monster of that rank dies (the Scroll of Forgetting, which gives back every point of one tree, is only found). The town portal is not an item: it is always available (balance.json townPortal).

equipment._comment: Equipment slots, in screen order. accepts = item slot types (bases' 'slot') that fit; the first one is the slot's own type, used when equipping with a double-click. offhand also takes a one-hand weapon: two weapons alternate their swings, but there is no guard and no Shield skills without a shield.

rarityChances._comment: Base chance per equipment item, tested in order unique → set → rare → magic. Multiplied by the monster rank's lootQualityMult and by (1 + magic find). A unique or set roll picks among the uniques/set items allowed at that item level (by weight); when none is allowed it becomes rare.

itemClasses._comment: What each base is. groups let an affix name a family (weapon, armor, jewelry) instead of each class. minRarity = the lowest rarity it drops at: rings and amulets are always at least magic (a plain one would be worth nothing).
